# Simplex midpoint support counts and a uniform canonical cap reserve

This is a bounded geometric theorem about two actual simplices and one point. It supplies explicit canonical cap information. It does not assert global depth, criticality of the canonical caps, or a reduction of arbitrary bodies to simplices.

**Archive provenance.** `candidate 986ab1688d049a3b` already proves a stronger half-row count at equal volumes, with positive coordinate margins and actual integrated endpoint credit. The full small-third-fiber conclusion for equal-volume large simplices is already proved in `candidate 499bc56f5e8f111d`. The present note is an alternative row-norm proof with the convenient rational thresholds `9/(8N)`, `16/25`, and `15/16`; it does not claim a new equal-volume small-third-fiber theorem or a new global mechanism from the same count.

## 1. Setup and determinant normalization

Let `d>=1`, put `N=d+1`, and let `K,B` be full-dimensional simplices in `R^d`, with volumes `k>0,b>0`. Let `p` be any point of `R^d`, not necessarily in `K`, and assume

`P=(B+p)/2 subset K`.

Let `lambda_1,...,lambda_N` be the affine barycentric coordinates of `K`. Write the vertices of `P` as `x_1,...,x_N` and form the matrix

`X_ij=lambda_i(x_j)`.

All its entries are nonnegative, and every column sums to one. If `beta=b/k`, then

`|det X|=|P|/|K|=beta/2^(N-1)`.                        (1)

For an explicit determinant proof, put the homogeneous columns `(v_i,1)` of the vertices of `K` into an invertible matrix `H_K`. The corresponding vertex matrix of `P` is `H_K X`. Their determinant ratio is the signed simplex-volume ratio, so absolute values give (1). Since `P` is full dimensional, `X` is invertible and all its row sums are positive.

The canonical centroid cap of `K` in row `i` is

`H_i={x:lambda_i(x)>=1/N}`.

Its `K`-volume is `Gamma_d k`, where `Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d`. We study which of these caps are reached by `P`, and how much actual `B` volume certain cap preimages contain.

## 2. A general row-norm estimate

Set `s_i=sum_j X_ij`; then `sum_i s_i=N`. Every entry of `X` is at most one. Thus

`sum_j X_ij^2 <= s_i`.

If a row has every entry at most `tau`, then its squared Euclidean norm is at most `tau s_i`. If `m` rows have that property, Hadamard's determinant inequality and arithmetic-geometric mean yield

`|det X|^2 <= tau^m product_i s_i <= tau^m`.              (2)

If those `m` rows instead have every entry strictly less than `tau`, and `m>0`, the first inequality is strict: each such row has positive sum and at least one positive entry, so its squared norm is strictly less than `tau s_i`.

This estimate retains the original matrix and the actual simplex-volume ratio; no sum over integer fibers or continuous approximation occurs.

## 3. At least one quarter of the centroid caps are reached

Let `r` be the number of rows with `max_j X_ij>=1/N`. If `beta=1`, then

`r/N>=1/4`.                                            (3)

For `N=2,3,4`, some row reaches `1/N` because every column has average entry `1/N`. Hence `r>=1`, which proves (3) in those cases.

For `N>=4`, the following elementary comparison is useful:

`N^(3N)>=2^(8(N-1))`.                                  (4)

There is equality at `N=4`. In passing from `N` to `N+1`, the ratio of the left side is

`(1+1/N)^(3N)(N+1)^3 >=4(N+1)^3>256`,

by the binomial theorem. This exceeds the ratio `2^8` on the right and proves (4) for all larger integers.

If `r<N/4`, then `m=N-r>3N/4` rows have entries strictly less than `1/N`. Equations (1)--(2) give

`4^(-(N-1)) < N^(-m) < N^(-3N/4) <=4^(-(N-1))`,

This contradicts the equality of the two ends of the chain, proving (3).

For `d>=2`, the fraction `1/4` is strictly larger than `Gamma_d/2`, since `Gamma_d<=4/9`. This is a count comparison only, not a mixed cap-mass conclusion.

## 4. The count survives a fixed unequal-volume window

In fact, (3) remains valid whenever

`beta>=16/25`.                                         (5)

The cases `N<=4` remain automatic. For `N=5`, failure of (3) means `r<=1`, so at least four rows have all entries strictly below `1/5`. Equation (2) gives

`beta^2/4^4<5^(-4)`, hence `beta<16/25`,

contradicting (5).

For `N>=6`, failure would give

`beta< t_N:=2^(N-1)/N^(3N/8)`.

The eighth power of `t_N` is the reciprocal of the ratio in (4), so its proof shows that `t_N` is strictly decreasing for integer `N>=4`. At `N=6`,

`t_6=32/6^(9/4)<16/25`,

because `6^9=10077696>6250000=50^4`. Therefore failure is impossible for every `N>=6` as well. This proves (5) without a dimension restriction or a limiting argument.

## 5. A uniform positive support margin at equal volumes

Now assume `beta=1` and `d>=2`, so `N>=3`. A stronger statement is

`#{i:max_j X_ij>9/(8N)} >=N/4`.                         (6)

Put `tau=9/(8N)` and let `r` count the rows with maximum strictly greater than `tau`. If `r<N/4`, then `m=N-r>3N/4` rows have maximum at most `tau`. Equation (2) applies without needing strict row inequalities.

For `N=3,4`, the assumed failure means `r=0`; all rows obey the smaller bound. The exact comparisons are

`(3/8)^3=27/512<1/16`,

`(9/32)^4=6561/1048576<1/64`.

These contradict `|det X|^2=4^(-(N-1))`.

For every `N>=5` we have the strict comparison

`(8N/9)^(3N)>2^(8(N-1))`.                              (7)

At `N=5`, clearing denominators gives the exact positive integer certificate

`40^15-2^32 9^15=189446145117066568400896>0`.

The successive ratio of the left side of (7), divided by the successive ratio of the right side, is

`(1+1/N)^(3N)[8(N+1)/9]^3/256`

` >=4[8(N+1)/9]^3/256 >=64/27>1`.

Thus (7) follows for all larger integers. Since `0<tau<1`, our assumed failure would now give

`|det X|^2<=tau^m<tau^(3N/4)<4^(-(N-1))`,

again a contradiction. This proves (6) with an explicit support margin `1/(8N)` beyond the centroid threshold.

### 5a. The same margin persists when beta>=15/16

The conclusion (6), with its unchanged threshold, also holds for

`beta>=15/16`.                                         (6a)

Here are complete integer certificates. Under the same failed-count assumption, use `m=N-r`, `tau=9/(8N)`, and the determinant lower bound `(15/16)^2 4^(-(N-1))`. For `N=3,4`, failure gives `m=N`; for `N=5`, it gives `m>=4`. The ratios of the corresponding upper bounds `tau^3,tau^4,tau^4` to that determinant lower bound are, respectively,

`24/25`, `729/1600`, `11664/15625`,

each strictly below one.

For `N>=6`, define the ratio using the weaker upper bound

`R_N=[9/(8N)]^(3N/4) / [(15/16)^2 4^(-(N-1))]`.

At `N=6` its fourth power is

`R_6^4=3^10/5^8=59049/390625<1`.

Moreover

`R_(N+1)^4/R_N^4`

` =256 / [(1+1/N)^(3N) (8(N+1)/9)^3] <1`

by the same binomial estimate used in (7). Thus `R_N<1` for every `N>=6`. The failed count would force the determinant below its lower bound, a contradiction. This proves (6a) for all dimensions stated, retaining exactly the same support margin.

## 6. An actual positive cap-volume reserve

Each row counted in (6), including the volume window (6a), satisfies the stronger geometric inequalities

`|P intersect H_i| > |P|/9^d`,

`|B intersect {x:lambda_i(x)>=2/N-lambda_i(p)}| > b/9^d`. (8)

To prove the first, let `h_i=max_P lambda_i>9/(8N)` and choose a maximizing vertex `v` of `P`. The factor

`t_i=1-1/(N h_i)>1/9`

is positive and less than one. Every point of `P` has nonnegative `lambda_i`, so the homothetic copy `(1-t_i)v+t_i P` lies in `P intersect H_i`. Its volume is `t_i^d|P|>|P|/9^d`. The map `x ->(x+p)/2` sends the second cap in (8) exactly to the first and scales volume by `2^(-d)`, proving the second inequality.

The threshold in the second line has a specific ambient meaning. Place the degenerate endpoint point at base `-1` and the simplex `B` at base `+1`. The ambient halfspace

`lambda_i(x)+(lambda_i(p)-1/N)z>=1/N`

passes through the ordinary centroid of the middle simplex at base zero and through `(-1,p)`. At base `+1` its trace is exactly the cap in (8). Thus the reserve retains one actual affine tilt. No cap orientation or endpoint contribution has been optimized independently.

## 7. Scope

The support-count statements require an actual simplex `B` as well as a simplex `K`; an arbitrary midpoint body cannot be replaced by its vertices in the determinant calculation. The point `p` is allowed anywhere provided the actual midpoint inclusion holds. The support margin and mass reserve are uniform over all such placements and shapes in the volume window `b/k>=15/16`, in a fixed dimension, with the printed constants explicit.

No positive-volume small endpoint has been substituted for `p` here. Turning these strict finite-direction reserves into a small-endpoint depth theorem requires a separate argument controlling actual source motion, all other directions and all tilts. The statements above do not themselves claim that step or full OC.
